title: Occupancy Adjustment for Excess Flood Renewals Over an NFIP Dwelling Form Policy
content:
For an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** renewal, the occupancy of the home is read from the primary-residence designation carried by the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy (NFIP Dwelling Form Flood Policies (Write Your Own)) beneath it.

**Rule.** The renewal occupancy adjustment reads the primary-residence designation of the NFIP policy of the home: a home that policy does not designate as the insured's primary residence carries a surcharge of 12 percent, a home it designates as the primary residence earns a credit of 3 percent, and where there is no NFIP policy of the home there is no occupancy adjustment.

The NFIP policy of the home is the Tidemark NFIP Dwelling Form policy in force whose policy number is the underlying policy number on the excess policy record, and the HomeFlood policy of the home is the active Tidemark HomeFlood policy whose policy number is that underlying policy number; of these two policies only their status, the NFIP policy's primary-residence designation, their claim payments and voided payments and the NFIP policy's applied Elevation Certificates are read. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

| Primary-residence designation on that NFIP policy | Adjustment entered (percent) |
|---|---|
| not designated a primary residence | 12, a surcharge of 12 percent |
| designated a primary residence | -3, a credit of 3 percent |
| no NFIP policy of the home | no occupancy adjustment |

Every percentage selected for a renewal term is added into one net adjustment percentage, which acts once on the zone-factored layer charge after the elevation multiplier — that charge is multiplied by one plus the net adjustment percentage — and never on the loss-of-use charge.

A designation the insured states on the call, or one carried by an excess or HomeFlood record, does not decide the adjustment; only the designation on the NFIP policy of the home does.
